title: Truncated polynomial presentation sections imply smoothness
statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $A$ be a commutative $R$-algebra, and let $\alpha:P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective $R$-algebra map, with $d\ge0$ finite [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be prime, set $Q=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, and let $p:C=P_Q\twoheadrightarrow S=A_{\mathfrak q}$ be the induced surjection [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $J=\ker p$ and $\mathfrak m=QC$, the maximal ideal of $C$. Suppose that for every integer $N\ge1$ the canonical map
$$C/(J^2+\mathfrak m^N)\longrightarrow C/(J+\mathfrak m^N)$$
has a section as an $R$-algebra map, for the structures induced from $C$. Then there exists $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $A_g$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Here $A_g$ is the ring of fractions with denominators powers of $g$, and having a section means having a right inverse.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1), after the truncated surjections have been split: conormal differential, Artin-Rees and smooth-at-point criterion.

proof.text: The given surjection exhibits $A$ as a finite type $R$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] to obtain finite presentation of $A/R$. The polynomial algebra $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $C=P_Q$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Thus $J$ is finitely generated by the definition [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Both $C$ and $S=A_{\mathfrak q}$ are local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; write $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS$ and $k=S/\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tags 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); setup of Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1).

proof.text: Verify formal smoothness of $C$ directly in the $0$-adic lifting definition [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Given $D$, an ideal $H$ with $H^2=0$, and an $R$-algebra map $C\to D/H$, choose lifts in $D$ of the images of the finitely many $t_i$. Evaluation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $P\to D$. For $s\in P\setminus Q$, its image modulo $H$ is a unit. If $u$ is its lifted image and $v$ lifts an inverse, $uv=1+h$ with $h\in H$, and $u\,v(1-h)=1$. Thus every denominator maps to a unit, and the fraction formula $a/s\mapsto\widetilde a\,\widetilde s^{-1}$ extends evaluation to an $R$-algebra lift $C\to D$. Also [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identify $\Omega_{C/R}$ with $C^{\oplus d}$, with basis $\mathrm dt_i$. In particular it is finite free, including when $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 00TI (definition-formally-smooth), Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize); localized polynomial presentation in Tag 02HT.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to the finite $C$-module $C$, its submodule $J$, and the ideal $\mathfrak m$. Choose its integer $c\ge0$ and put $N=c+2$. Then $N\ge2$ and $\mathfrak m^N\cap J\subseteq\mathfrak m^{N-c}J=\mathfrak m^2J\subseteq\mathfrak mJ$. Use the section hypothesis for this $N$. This does not require that sections for different exponents be compatible.

source.place: Tag 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees), applied as in Tag 02HT, proof of (4) implies (1), paragraph beginning By Artin-Rees.

proof.text: Set $M=J/J^2$, $T=S\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}$ and $\delta:M\to T$, $[j]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dj$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-section-conormal-residue-kernel] to $C\twoheadrightarrow S$, the exponent $N$, the containment of step 3, and the chosen $R$-algebra section. Its conclusion is exactly $\delta(x)\in\mathfrak nT\Rightarrow x\in\mathfrak nM$. Therefore the induced map $M/\mathfrak nM\to T/\mathfrak nT$ has zero kernel and is injective. The elementary isomorphism $k\otimes_SU\cong U/\mathfrak nU$ sends $\bar r\otimes u$ to $ru\bmod\mathfrak nU$, with inverse $[u]\mapsto1\otimes u$; the tensor relations show these are well defined and inverse. These formulas carry $1_k\otimes\delta$ to the preceding quotient map. Hence $1_k\otimes\delta$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), truncated conormal map and Artin-Rees paragraph; residue-field specialization, as implemented by Algebra.truncated_section_conormal_residue_kernel.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-formally-smooth-local-residue-conormal] with the actual surjection $p:C\twoheadrightarrow S$. Its hypotheses hold: $S$ is local and $J$ is finitely generated by step 1, $C/R$ is formally smooth with finite free $\Omega_{C/R}$ by step 2, and its residue conormal differential is injective by step 4. The criterion gives formal smoothness of $S=A_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 031I (lemma-characterize-formally-smooth-again) and the local finite-free residue criterion; Mathlib/RingTheory/Smooth/Local.lean, Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_injective_lTensor_residueField.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sfb-formally-smooth-prime-neighbourhood] to the finitely presented algebra $A/R$ of step 1 and the formal smoothness of $A_{\mathfrak q}/R$ obtained in step 5. It gives $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ and smoothness of $A_g/R$, which is the asserted conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_smooth_away_of_truncated_polynomial_sections {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [IsNoetherianRing R] (d : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] A) (hα : Function.Surjective α) (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] (J : Ideal (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap α.toRingHom))) (hJ : J = RingHom.ker (Localization.localAlgHom (q.comap α.toRingHom) q α rfl).toRingHom) (hsections : ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → ∃ σ : (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap α.toRingHom) ⧸ (J ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap α.toRingHom)) ^ N)) →ₐ[R] (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap α.toRingHom) ⧸ (J ^ 2 ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap α.toRingHom)) ^ N)), (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R (sup_le_sup (Ideal.pow_le_self (by decide : 2 ≠ 0)) le_rfl)).comp σ = AlgHom.id R _) : ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away g)
